tasks.short: Count supplies in the store room, write the order list, decide what to order within budget, place orders with suppliers, check deliveries, and arrange services such as repairs.

steps.what: Service supervisor counts supplies in the store room
Service supervisor writes the list of necessary supplies and equipment
Service supervisor decides what to order and checks the budget
Service supervisor requisitions the supplies from suppliers by phone or e-mail
Service supervisor checks deliveries against the order
Service supervisor arranges services such as repairs and cleaning by phone

tasks.design: Shelves in the store room carry minimum and maximum levels, so the supervisor counts only items near the line. The purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}) proposes an order from those counts and usual use, with the budget left this month shown next to it. Once the supervisor has decided, the order goes to the supplier electronically, and deliveries are ticked off against it on a tablet. Arranging repairs and cleaning stays by phone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every shelf was counted and orders were written and phoned in by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Purchasing systems propose orders from stock levels and send them to suppliers.
tasks.still_hard: Busy weeks empty shelves faster than the usual use suggests.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a treatment product is about to become popular.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor approves proposed orders instead of building them.

evidence.claim: Purchasing systems can propose orders from minimum levels and send them to suppliers electronically.

assumptions: Boundary: from the store room to deliveries checked and services booked; paying invoices is outside.
Input contract: supplier catalogues and prices in the purchasing system; budget from finance; fallback is counting and phoning.
Deciding orders and arranging services stay with the supervisor.

incremental.description: Service supervisor adjusts minimum levels after busy weeks.

approvals.approved_version: The order as decided by the supervisor within budget in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small location with few supplies; high: many products ordered every week.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan promotions with the manager, write promotional texts, post them on social media and send the newsletter, talk to customers about offers, and count responses.

steps.what: Service supervisor plans promotions and customer recruitment efforts with the manager
Service supervisor writes advertising texts for social media and the newsletter

loop.input: The promotion record with offer, price, dates and audience, and earlier posts in the house style.
loop.output: Draft texts for a social post and a newsletter item.
loop.check: Code checks every price and date in the text matches the promotion record; the supervisor edits and approves each text.
loop.stop: Stops when the supervisor approves, or after two redrafts the supervisor writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each promotion needs new wording; a fixed template repeats the same sentence every time.

steps.what: Service supervisor posts on social media and sends the newsletter
Service supervisor talks to customers about current offers
Service supervisor counts responses to the promotion in a tally sheet

tasks.design: Each promotion is recorded once with its offer, price, dates and promo code. A bounded step drafts the social post and newsletter item from that record; code checks prices and dates, and once the supervisor has edited and approved the texts they are scheduled on social media ({SOCIAL}) and in the newsletter tool ({MARKETING_AUTOMATION}). Bookings with the promo code are counted by the booking system. Planning promotions and talking to customers stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Texts were written from scratch and responses counted on a tally sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft short promotional texts; booking systems count promo codes.
tasks.still_hard: Local customers respond to personal invitations more than posts.
tasks.human_edge: Asking a regular to bring a friend next time.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor edits drafted texts instead of writing from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether promo code counts show which offers work.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft short promotional texts from an offer description.
Commercial e-mail newsletters need the recipient's prior consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from quiet periods to promotion results; pricing policy is outside.
Input contract: offers agreed with the manager; newsletter list with consent kept in the newsletter tool; fallback is writing by hand.
Planning and talking to customers do not change.
No customer data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of the drafted text does the supervisor change?

already_counted.description: Service supervisor edits and approves drafted texts.

incremental.description: Service supervisor sets up promo codes in the booking system.

approvals.approved_version: The texts as edited and approved by the supervisor in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one or two promotions a year; high: monthly promotions on several channels.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The service supervisor keeps deciding orders, arranging services, planning promotions and talking to customers; counting every shelf, writing orders, writing texts from scratch and tallying responses shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who spends saved time with customers and staff.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
